provenance.notes: Two independent channels. (1) BEHAVIOUR: four live captures, one FRESH editor process per capture, driven through an isolated virtual display with the pointer injected over the remote-framebuffer channel and each undo typed into the reference's command field; every undo was independently confirmed to have executed in the reference's own executed-command history before its effect was read. (2) MECHANISM: a breakpoint on the single machine instruction in the whole shipped engine that increments its undo-entry counter, read live under a debugger attached by process id, plus a static symbol read that located that instruction with no engine running at all. All geometry readback is read-only.

question: Task 2640 measured that a COMMITTED transform gesture whose delta is EMPTY still costs undo steps, and left two questions open: does a tool from another family behave the same, and what does arming a tool and dropping it WITHOUT any gesture cost in each of the two stack shapes?

candidates.a: The law and its number are both general: any committed gesture with an empty delta costs the same 2 undo steps, in every family.
candidates.b: The LAW is general but the NUMBER is family-specific: a committed empty-delta gesture is never free, but how many steps it costs depends on the tool.
candidates.c: The law is transform-specific: a family whose operation is topological records nothing when its gesture produces no topology.

law: A COMMITTED GESTURE COSTS UNDO STEPS EVEN WHEN IT CHANGED NOTHING, IN EVERY TOOL FAMILY -- BUT THE COST IS PER TOOL, NOT A CONSTANT. A press-move-release that never leaves the press pixel leaves the mesh byte-identical and still records: 2 undo steps for a transform-handle haul (task 2640) and 1 for a cutting tool, against ZERO for an otherwise identical run with no button press. The reason is mechanical: an undo entry is created when a NON-EMPTY undo block is closed, by machinery -- the toolpipe's own gesture block, the post-mode auto-apply, and the tool-drop command -- that is shared by every family and never inspects the result. So the recording decision keys on 'did anything register an undoable action', not on 'did the mesh change'. ARMING A TOOL AND DROPPING IT WITHOUT EVER ENGAGING IT COSTS ONE UNDO STEP, AND THAT STEP IS BOUGHT BY THE ARM, NOT BY THE DROP: dropping a tool that was never engaged, and the whole pointer path around it, register NOTHING, while arming the tool through the editor's own command channel records one entry the way any other command invocation does. The number does NOT depend on what lies beneath it: one over a preceding model edit and one over another tool-lifecycle region alike.

rig.stand: A cube subdivided once per axis. THREE DISJOINT four-vertex sets -- top corners, bottom corners, mid-height corners -- never one set moved three times: a set that has already moved carries its gizmo away from the centre of frame and the handle localiser latches onto interface furniture instead.
rig.shape: E1 = a real committed drag of the top set. E2 = a real committed drag of the bottom set, and the state the undo walk starts from. N = the gesture under test, driven with the CUTTING tool at a raw viewport pixel (that family draws no handle to localise). Then ten undos, reading the full mesh after every one.
rig.reading: kB = the index of the undo that reverts E2. Everything stacked above E2 is geometry-silent and IDENTICAL in every run, so it cancels. entries(N) = kB(N) - kB(control).
rig.second_instrument: A breakpoint on the one instruction that increments the engine's undo-entry counter, attached AFTER the stand is built and the tool armed, so the window contains the gesture and nothing else. This counts entries with NO undo walk at all, and its backtrace NAMES each entry's creator.
rig.aim_calibration: The press pixel was CALIBRATED, not guessed: the projection was read off a calibration run's screenshot and confirmed against the reference's own logged cut-line endpoints -- world origin at pixel (880,561), 414 px per world unit, 3-D pane x in [258,1195]. A first aim at x=200 was the tool-properties panel; the tool never engaged there and the cell was void.
validity_checks: The component selection is identical before and after N in EVERY run, so no press ever re-picked geometry.
The positive control drives a real cut from the SAME press pixel with the SAME press choreography.
Every undo in every run reported that it executed, with zero retries.
The four specs are byte-identical except ONE step, and only that step's gesture/length keys -- asserted by a programmatic diff.

instrument_calibration.reads_zero: the control run, which performs the whole gesture path -- tool arm, pointer move onto the press pixel, tool drop, geometry read -- with NO button press; it reads 0 on the undo count AND 0 on the debugger's entry counter; and for the arm-and-drop half, a run with NO region at all, whose undo walk starts directly on the previous edit
instrument_calibration.reads_nonzero: the positive control, a real committed cut, at 1 undo step and 39 low-level entries; and on the transform family the same instrument reads 37 low-level entries for a real haul; and for the arm-and-drop half, the same two regions with the second one really engaged, at 4 undo steps against 1
instrument_calibration.why_both_are_needed: A control that cannot read zero makes every non-zero unfalsifiable; a rig with no positive control cannot show it would have seen an entry at all.

cases.entries_recorded_against: NOT A SUBTRACTION between two cells of this list. Derived instead from the absolute count above the second real edit, which is the undo index minus one: the cutting control run and the transform baseline BOTH read index 2, i.e. one entry each, but over different regions -- an arm-and-drop in the one, a selection change in the other. Subtracting their indices from each other is meaningless and would give 0.
cases.note: DERIVED from runs already frozen for this fixture, with no new capture: the cutting family's control run and the transform baseline share a byte-identical prefix and a byte-identical undo block, and differ above the second real edit only in that one carries a selection change and the other an arm-and-drop region. Both read the same index, and the selection change is independently worth one step, so the cutting family's arm-and-drop is worth one step too. The arm is charged in EVERY family measured.

decomposition.measured: An undo entry is created exactly when a NON-EMPTY undo block is closed, at a single site shared by the whole engine. The entries a committed gesture creates come from three creators, and the SET is identical in both families measured: (1) the toolpipe's own gesture block, closed on the pointer event and NOT a command at all -- which is why a gesture that cost two undo steps showed only one line in the reference's command log; (2) the post-mode auto-apply command; (3) the tool-drop command. What differs per family is only the MULTIPLICITY: a transform zero-distance gesture makes 1+1+1 = 3 blocks, a cutting one 2+2+1 = 5, and a real haul 18 + 18 + 1 = 37.
decomposition.not_measured: Which of those blocks group into which user-visible undo step. One undo pops a GROUP, and the grouping could not be separated on this drive path because typing the undo into the command field pushes blocks of its own between the pops.
decomposition.channel_boundary: THE TWO CHANNELS DISAGREE ON THE ABSOLUTE COST OF AN ARM-AND-DROP, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS A REGION BOUNDARY, NOT A CONTRADICTION. The undo-walk channel priced a region that BEGINS with the arm and reads 1. The debugger channel attached only AFTER the tool was already armed, so its window contains the wake keystroke, the pointer move and the drop and nothing else, and reads 0. Both are right about what they bracketed. The one step therefore belongs to the ARM, by elimination: the region logged exactly one command -- the arm -- and every other act inside it was directly measured at zero on the finer instrument, which read 3 and 37 on positive controls in the same session. A third, command-only channel priced an arm on its own at three low-level blocks, which the grouping collapses into the one user-visible step seen here. The half both channels DID measure over the same region -- whether the cost depends on what lies beneath -- agrees exactly: 1 against 1, 0 against 0, +4 against +4.

assertions_for_a_port: A committed gesture that produced no change MUST leave something on the undo stack, in EVERY tool family: the first undo after it must NOT revert the edit that preceded it.
That undo must succeed and must leave the mesh byte-identical -- it is silent, not refused.

The COST is per tool and must not be hard-coded as a single constant: a transform-handle haul with an empty delta costs 2 undo steps and a cutting gesture with an empty delta costs 1, on the same rig and the same instrument.

A tool that is armed and then dropped WITHOUT ever being engaged must cost exactly ONE undo step when the arm is driven as a command, and that step must be charged to the ARM: the drop of a tool that was never engaged, and the pointer path around it, must register nothing. The number must be the SAME in both stack shapes -- over a preceding model edit and over another armed-and-dropped region alike.

The predicate is 'did anything register an undoable action', not 'did the mesh change'. A gesture that engaged the tool records even with an empty delta; a drop of a tool that was never engaged records nothing.
not_measured: Which entries group into which user-visible undo step -- see decomposition.not_measured.
The entries' user-visible names or grouping labels.
Redo. Not driven; the redo leg is unreadable on this drive path (task 2640, gap 2) and no claim is made here.
A committed gesture of FULL magnitude whose result is empty, in the cutting family: the cell intended for it cut the mesh anyway. Only the zero-distance flavour of an empty delta is measured here.
The OTHER flavour of an empty delta -- a gesture that moved and returned to its origin. Still NOT reachable through injected pointer transport (task 2640); needs a hand-driven gesture.
Deforming, creating and painting families beyond the two measured; the MECHANISM argument covers them (the record site is family-agnostic and no tool code reaches it) but no cell was driven.

A cell that isolates the ARM on its own, behaviourally. Charging the one step to the arm rests on elimination -- the region logged exactly one command and the debugger priced every other act in it at zero -- not on a region that contains only the arm. The obvious such cell would leave the tool ARMED across the undo walk, and an undo is itself a model-class act that drops an armed tool, so that cell measures a different thing.

Whether an arm driven as a bare interface keystroke, rather than as a command, is also worth a step. The debugger's zero covers a wake keystroke sent to a tool that was ALREADY armed, which is not the same act.
